raw_text:
Here is a structured 12-week upper-body focused program for a 29-year-old female recreational climber with a right subacromial impingement (SIS) cleared for pain-free range and no overhead loading. The plan emphasizes scapular stability, rotator cuff endurance, and gradual exposure to climbing-specific loads while protecting the subacromial space. It integrates strength, mobility, and climbing-specific conditioning, with progression by week and clear sets/reps. It also includes guidelines for nutrition, recovery, and monitoring symptoms.

Assumptions and goals
- Pain-free ROM allowed; avoid any painful overhead loading or positions that reproduce impingement.
- Climbing-specific goals: maintain grip strength, scapular control, rotator cuff endurance, and overall shoulder health to support better up-tick in climbing performance.
- Gym access: full gym with cable machines, free weights, resistance bands, pull-up bar, rowers, etc.

Program overview
- Frequency: 4 days/week upper-body focused, plus 1–2 optional conditioning or mobility days. 1–2 climbing-specific technique days can be incorporated on non-strength days if desired, avoiding overhead loading on days with shoulder sensitivity.
- Structure per week (typical pattern): 
  - Day A: Scapular/MRC (rotator cuff) + horizontal pulling + anti-rotator cuff/core
  - Day B: Push/puller balance without overhead loading + rotator cuff endurance
  - Day C: Lower intensity mobility, rotator cuff control, and grip strength (no overhead)
  - Day D: Closed-chain stabilization, posterior chain emphasis, and climb-specific strength work in protected ranges
- Phase approach: 4 phases across 12 weeks
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Baseline strength, scapular stability, light loading, no overhead pressing; build technique and pain-free range.
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Gradual loading with controlled overhead-to-shoulder friendly angles (e.g., landmine press with neutral grip, incline pressing avoided if painful). Increase volume modestly.
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Build endurance and resistance to higher loads with more controlled climber-specific movements; maintain pain-free status.
  - Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Peak upper-body capacity with higher tolerances, slow progression toward some overhead-facing load angles if cleared by physio; continue controlling pain.

Weekly structure (sample for non-climbing days)
- Warm-up (8–12 minutes): light cardio 5 min, dynamic shoulder/peri-scapular mobility, banded warm-up (external rotations, face pulls, serratus punches), activation (scapular sets, quadruped arm raises with emphasis on stability).
- Main lifts: emphasize technique, pain-free ROM, and controlled tempo (2–0–2–0 or 3–0–3–0 depending on exercise).
- Conditioning finisher: 5–10 minutes of grip and forearm endurance drills (farmer’s carries, dead hangs with time limit, pinches) at comfortable intensity.

Phase 1: Foundations (Weeks 1–3)
Goals: establish shoulder movement quality, scapular control, rotator cuff endurance, and tolerable loading.

Weeks 1–3 split (sample, 4 days/week)
- Day A: Scapular Stability + Horizontal Pull
  - Warm-up: banded pull-aparts 2x15, serratus anterior activation 2x12, scapular push-ups 2x12
  - External Rotation: Dumbbell external rotation 2–3 sets x 12–15 reps (neutral/side-lying)
  - Cable Rows: 3x12 with light weight, emphasis on scapular retraction without shrug
  - Dumbbell Floor Press (neutral grip): 3x12-15 (limit ROM to pain-free range)
  - Push-up variations (knees or elevated): 3x8–12, control scapular depression
  - Finisher: Farmer’s carry 3 rounds x 30–40 m with light weights
- Day B: Scapular Mobility + Anti-rotator Cuff
  - Warm-up: thoracic mobility, banded external rotation 2x15, scapular wall slides 2x12
  - Isometric Y/T/W with light bands: 3x12 each
  - Lat Pulldown (neutral grip, short range): 3x12, avoid high elbow flexion if painful
  - Dumbbell Pullover (light, if tolerated): 2x12
  - Pallof Press (v to light resistance): 3x12 per side
  - Grip work: plate pinches 2x15–20 seconds
- Day C: Horizontal Push / Stability
  - Warm-up: push-up plus shoulder taps 2x10, band-resisted internal rotation
  - Barbell or Dumbbell Bench (pain-free ROM, avoid shoulder elevation beyond 90 degrees): 3x10
  - Incline Dumbbell Press (if pain-free, shallow angle; otherwise modify to floor press): 3x10
  - Band-resisted face pulls: 3x15
  - Ring/DB row or supported row: 3x12
  - Core: side planks 3x30–45 seconds per side
- Day D: Closed-chain & Grip
  - Warm-up: wrist and elbow mobility, scapular push-ups 2x12
  - Barbell or Dumbbell Floor Press or Neutral-grip press: 3x12
  - Dip station/triceps dips (assisted or partial): 3x8–10
  - Prone Y exercise with light dumbbells: 3x12
  - Dead hangs orree: 3 x 15–30 seconds (if tolerated)
  - Forearm/Grip finisher: fat grip holds 2x20 seconds

Notes for Phase 1
- Avoid overhead pressing beyond pain-free ROM. If any exercise induces impingement, reduce range or substitute.
- RPE targets: 5–6/10 for most sets; 7–8 for occasional working sets only if pain-free.
- Mobility work daily: thoracic extension/rotation, pec minor stretch, doorway stretch, sleeper stretch (if tolerated), 5–10 minutes.

Phase 2: Gradual loading (Weeks 4–6)
Goals: introduce controlled overhead-friendly loading and increase volume modestly; continue scapular control.

Weeks 4–6 split (sample)
- Day A: Rotator Cuff Endurance + Horizontal Pull
  - Warm-up: same as Phase 1
  - Side-lying external rotations: 3x15
  - Seated cable rows (low to mid row): 4x12
  - Dumbbell Floor Press or Landmine Press (neutral grip, safe angle): 3x12
  - Push-ups with scapular depression: 3x10–12
  - Face pulls with higher rep: 3x15–20
- Day B: Pressing under control + Rows
  - Warm-up: banded shoulder prehab
  - Incline Dumbbell Press (gentle incline, 30–45 degrees if tolerated): 3x10–12
  - Neutral-grip Dumbbell Shoulder Press (very light; if any overhead pain occurs, stop): 3x8–10
  - Bent-over Barbell Row or Chest-supported Row: 3x12
  - Pallof Press with longer lever: 3x12 per side
  - Grip work: farmer’s carry 3x40 m
- Day C: Mobility + Low-load Shoulder Strength
  - Warm-up: thoracic mobility, scapular setting
  - Low-load isometrics (static holds at mid-range shoulders): 3x20–30 seconds
  - External rotation with cable at 0–30 degrees abduction: 3x12
  - Prone Cobra: 3x15
  - Band-resisted shoulder extension and flexion: 3x12
  - Core: dead bug variations: 3x12
- Day D: Climb-focused & Posterior Chain
  - Warm-up: scapular rotation, scapular push-ups
  - Horizontal pull-ups or ring rows: 4x8–12
  - Dumbbell or Cable Lat Pulldown (neutral grip, short range if painful): 3x12
  - Dumbbell Z-press avoided due to overhead; instead use landmine press or safety press at safe angle: 3x10
  - Core and elbow-friendly elbow flexion work: bicep curls with controlled tempo: 3x12

Phase 3: Endurance and tolerances (Weeks 7–9)
Goals: increase time under tension, climbing-adjacent loads, improve scapular control and endurance.

Weeks 7–9 split
- Day A: Vertical pulling + Scapular Stability
  - Warm-up: rope climbs or rack pulls light if climbing; scapular push-ups
  - Lat Pulldown (neutral): 4x10–12
  - Cable Row (high to mid): 4x12
  - Dumbbell Floor Press (paused): 3x10
  - Band-resisted face pulls: 3x15
  - Serratus anterior activation: 3x12
- Day B: Controlled Overhead Accommodation
  - Warm-up: banded external rotation, thoracic mobility
  - Landmine press (neutral grip) or incline press: 4x10
  - Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press (light): 3x10
  - Pull-over or low-row variations: 3x12
  - Pallof Press: 3x12 per side
  - Grip: farmers 3x60 seconds
- Day C: Mobility + Endurance
  - Warm-up: mobility flow
  - Cuban press (light, watch for impingement): 3x12
  - Prone Y/T/W: 3x12
  - Elevated feet push-ups: 3x12
  - Forearm endurance: static hangs 3x20–40 seconds (progress with grip)
- Day D: Climb-focused Endurance
  - Warm-up: climbing-specific scapular activation
  - Ring rows or assisted pull-ups: 4x8–12
  - Towel or rope pull-throughs (safety): 3x12
  - Dumbbell or cable external rotation in 0–20 degrees abduction: 3x15
  - Core and mobility finisher: 10 minutes

Phase 4: Load tolerance and consolidation (Weeks 10–12)
Goals: higher tolerance to loads within safe ranges, maintain mechanics, and prepare for typical climbing demands.

Weeks 10–12 split
- Day A: Strength + Stability
  - Warm-up: thorough scapular activation
  - Lat pulldown (neutral grip, controlled): 4x8–10
  - Barbell or dumbbell row: 4x8–10
  - Dumbbell floor press or incline press: 4x8–10
  - Face pulls: 3x15
  - Pallof press: 3x12 per side
- Day B: Overload-Protected Overhead Alternatives
  - Warm-up: scapular and rotator cuff activation
  - Landmine press or neutral-grip incline press: 4x8–10
  - Seated overhead press with strict control only if pain-free and approved by physio: 3x6–8 (or avoid and substitute)
  - Bent-over reverse fly: 3x12
  - Renegade rows (modified to avoid shoulder pain): 3x8–10
- Day C: Mobility, Endurance, and Grip
  - Warm-up: mobility work
  - Isometric holds in mid-range (external rotations): 3x20–30 seconds
  - Cable or banded external rotation at 0–15 degrees abduction: 3x12
  - Forearm and grip finsher: farmer’s carry 3x60 seconds
  - Light core work: 3x12–15
- Day D: Climbing Specific Prep
  - Warm-up: scapular work
  - Ring rows or assisted pull-ups: 4x8–12
  - Grip strength: plate pinches 2x30–40 seconds
  - Thoracic mobility and scapular orientation drills
  - Clip of climbing technique or technique-focused drills in bouldering setting avoiding overhead strain, emphasize footwork and body positioning

Progression and load management
- Progress the sets by 1–2 reps or 1–2 kg weight when current sets feel easy at the top end of prescribed reps with proper form and no pain.
- If any exercise reproduces pain, revert to the previous week’s load and reduce ROM or substitute with a pain-free alternative.
- Rate of perceived exertion (RPE): aim for 6–7/10 on most work sets; occasional 7–8/10 in early phases if pain-free.

Climbing integration and conditioning
- Aim to climb 1–2 times per week as long as the sessions do not aggravate SIS.
- Climb on days with lighter shoulder loads; avoid dynamic overhead moves on days after heavy upper-body training.
- If climbing volume increases, ensure at least 24 hours between heavy upper-body sessions and climb sessions.

Mobility and recovery
- Daily mobility: 10 minutes of thoracic spine mobility, pec minor stretches, and shoulder capsule mobility (posterior capsule stretch as tolerated).
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours per night.
- Nutrition: support recovery with adequate protein (1.6–2.2 g/kg/day), balanced carbs around training, and a modest caloric intake based on goals. Hydration to support muscle function.

Rehabilitation and red flags
- If painful impingement symptoms flare (sharp pain in subacromial space, weakness, or inability to perform pain-free ROM), reduce volume, avoid overhead loading, and consult the physiotherapist. Do not push through significant pain.
- If symptoms persist beyond a week of adjusted load, consider a temporary drop in intensity or a return to Phase 1 exercises and re-evaluate progress.

Example progression tracking
- Week 1: Base loads per exercise as defined; emphasis on technique and pain-free ROM.
- Week 4: Increase by small increments (2–4 reps or 2–5 kg for compound lifts) if pain-free.
- Week 7: Maintain or increase reps while holding load steady; introduce mild overhead-friendly variations (neutral grip landmine press) if cleared.
- Week 10–12: Increase overall weekly training load modestly; maintain focus on technique, scapular control, and pain-free ROM.

Optional adjuncts
- Mobility or activation routines can be scaled to time constraints.
- If pain-free overhead work is approved by the clinician, gradually reintroduce overhead pressing with strict form and limited ROM.

If you want, I can tailor exact weights, reps, and exercise substitutions to your client’s equipment availability, injury status, and climbing goals, and provide a week-by-week table with precise numbers.
